description.value: Kissa Tanto is an intimate Japanese-Italian fusion restaurant occupying the upper floor of a heritage building in Vancouver's Chinatown, blending the delicate flavours of Japan with the warmth of Italian cooking. The menu features dishes like charcoal udon with dungeness crab, yuzu tagliatelle with hand-cut Wagyu, and elegant crudos, alongside sake, Barolo, and classic cocktails. The room is deliberately small — a single large table seating a maximum of six — making it a memorable destination for cyclists seeking a special post-ride dinner in a historic neighbourhood.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content confirms Kissa Tanto is an active, operating Japanese-Italian fusion restaurant in Vancouver's Chinatown, consistent with the OSM record (name, cuisine, location). No cyclist-specific amenities — bike parking, water refill, washrooms, takeout, Wi-Fi — are mentioned anywhere on the website, so all amenity fields default to null per absence-of-evidence rules. The OSM check_date of 2024-01-09 and the live reservation system and menu on the website confirm the business is open.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, active restaurant with a live website, current menu, and operational reservation system. A notable dining destination in Vancouver's Chinatown useful to touring cyclists seeking an evening meal.
enrichment_extras.notes: The restaurant is on the upper floor of the building, which may affect accessibility for cyclists carrying gear. The dining room seats a maximum of 6 people and is reservation-only; walk-ins are unlikely to be accommodated.
